title: Safe Orchestrator: transactional apply/rollback bridge for Optimize automation
creator: Asha Patel
description: We need a hardened orchestration bridge that lets Redwood Optimize safely push batching/caching recommendations into customer config with clear guardrails for retries and rollbacks. Current recommendation suggestions are generated but applying them is brittle under retries, partially-applied states, and cross-service failures. This ticket scopes the API endpoints, webhook semantics, and SDK primitives required to make automated apply operations deterministic, auditable, and automatically recoverable.
acceptance_criteria: Public REST endpoint /optimize/v1/apply accepts signed apply requests and returns a stable operation ID
Webhook consumer semantics documented: ack/nack semantics, retry window, and idempotency-key behavior
Server-side coordinator guarantees exactly-one final commit of a recommendation or triggers documented rollback within 5 minutes on failure
Client SDK exposes applyWithLease(...) primitive that returns committed config version or explicit rollback reason
Integration tests cover concurrent duplicate apply attempts and simulate transient failures with deterministic outcomes
Audit log entries written for every phase (preflight, apply, commit, rollback) with trace-id correlation
tasks: API: design POST /optimize/v1/apply with body schema, idempotency_key, dry_run flag, and commitment_token
Controller: implement server-side coordinator that implements a two-phase apply with preflight dry-run and commit/abort steps
Webhooks: define callback schema for success/failure and implement at-least-once delivery with exponential backoff and DLQ
SDK: add client helper applyWithLease(language libs) that handles token signing, retries, and transparent rollback invocation
DB: extend config_store schema to support pending_apply metadata (operation_id, lease_expiry, attempted_commits)
Observability: add per-operation metrics (apply_attempts, commit_latency, rollback_count) and a dashboard tile
Tests: unit + e2e harness that injects RPC failures, DB contention, and partial RPC timeouts
Docs: author runbook for oncall and a developer guide for Integrations team
decisions: Use a signed commitment_token (HMAC with service key) rather than opaque opaque tickets so we can verify request provenance without DB lookups
Coordinator will implement a short-lived lease (default 90s) to fence concurrent executors; expired leases trigger a safe rollback path
Preflight dry-run will execute the same code-paths as commit but without persistent state mutation; diffs produced become part of the operation metadata
Idempotency strategy: idempotency_key dedupe at controller layer + versioned writes using conditional DB compare-and-set to ensure linearizable commits
Webhooks will include a monotonic sequence number per operation so receivers can detect out-of-order deliveries and request a replay
DLQ retention: failed apply operations held for 30 days with a manual retry API for support teams
technical_notes: We observed flaky behavior when apply requests are retried while a previous executor is in mid-commit; fencing with leases prevents double-commit but requires careful handling of partially written artifacts
Leases should be renewed by executors when long-running model tests are required; default behavior is to fail fast and rollback if lease cannot be acquired
We will use the existing event-store stream to append operation lifecycle events (preflight_ok, preflight_fail, commit_started, commit_ok, rollback_started, rollback_ok) for audit and replay
Apply operations must be reversible; all mutations need compensating steps or snapshot checkpoints to support deterministic rollback
To avoid customer-facing flapping, on failure offer an automatic fallback to a conservative config profile (smaller batch sizes / disabled cache) while alerting the owner
notes_for_reviewers: Review the preflight->commit state machine carefully; race conditions are easy to miss when leases expire mid-commit
Validate that the signed commitment_token approach meets security team's token lifecycle guidelines
Ensure SDK ergonomics don't leak low-level retry semantics to customers; keep high-level helpers that are opinionated
